rules.name: One readable idea
rules.text: Build each special around a recognizable character reference and a dominant silhouette. Use a few distinctive construction details rather than an anonymous block or unrelated decorative noise.

rules.name: Perform the action
rules.text: The body and prop should anticipate, act decisively, follow through, and recover together. Match deformation and emission to each beat. A multi-beat description needs distinct visible beats and a stronger finish.

rules.name: Respect material and construction
rules.text: Rigid components keep their shape and internal spacing; flexible material deforms between its attachments. Separate silhouette, structural regions, and surface detail. Leave actual gaps between repeated details; an opaque foreground row must not cover the construction it describes. For an unrotated repeated stripe, its full width is twice its half-size.

rules.name: Design for the match camera
rules.text: Prioritize silhouette, contrasting structural regions, then fine detail. Main forms need a dark boundary and bright readable accents. Details that shrink to hairlines should become thicker or simpler, including on a phone-sized view. Use depth deliberately so important effects appear in front of the body instead of inside it.

rules.name: Make particles part of the action
rules.text: Choose a recognizable, connected fragment shape that belongs to this move. Give it enough thickness and contrast to read against busy scenery. Emit where the action occurs, let fragments depart and fall independently, then fade. Sparse should mean intentional, not invisible.

rules.name: Show honest danger
rules.text: Strong active cues follow the real hit region and its lifetime. Decorative trails may linger more quietly. Never seek the opponent or draw a contact explosion without real contact. Keep the fighter readable.

rules.name: Preserve identity across contexts
rules.text: Ground and air versions share an idea, with deliberate stance, timing and motion differences. Neutral, recovery and down specials have distinct roles. Aerial spectacle must fit its usable duration.

cases.name: Weird Al
cases.error: Aerial neutral delivered 7% in the native contact probe instead of its authored 14%. Validation stopped at that failure.
